blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We present AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, a mixture-of-experts language model with 80 billion total parameters and approximately 3 billion active parameters per token, trained from scratch at Yandex and released under the Apache 2.0 license. The model combines Kimi Delta Attention with full attention, uses Attention Residuals, and is trained with Muon. Training comprises general pretraining on 17.5 trillion tokens, two context-extension stages, and a dedicated stage for reasoning and agentic interaction. We describe the data collection and augmentation pipelines, evaluation protocols, architectural ablations, and scaling-law experiments. We identify the limitations of held-out training loss as a proxy for downstream performance and introduce an auxiliary loss on mixture-of-experts outputs to stabilize training at the predicted learning rate. Domain-specific data selection and augmentation improve factual knowledge, mathematics, and programming skills, while agent trajectories introduced during pretraining improve performance on agentic benchmarks after supervised fine-tuning. In zero-shot reasoning evaluation, the model achieves leading results among open base models of comparable size, with 88.7% pass@8 on IMO-AnswerBench and 82.9% pass@8 on LiveCodeBench v5-v6. To evaluate Russian-language factual knowledge, we introduce and release two benchmarks with their evaluation protocols: WikiWebFacts, which tests short factual questions drawn from encyclopedic sources and search queries, and HardMultiQA, which tests more demanding factual questions inspired by user interactions. Our model scores 86.5% on WikiWebFacts and 67.9% on HardMultiQA, compared with 83.2% and 65.4% for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base (284B total and 13B active parameters) and 72.8% and 54.5% for Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base (120B total and 12B active parameters), outperforming both larger models on these benchmarks.

Specifically we quantify the contributions of the corpus, architecture,
and hyperparameters through sequential ablation experiments, training
each configuration from scratch on 2 trillion tokens. We also report
experiments that yielded no performance gains. Our evaluation analysis
examines prompt sensitivity, automated grading, and how well base-model
evaluations predict performance after post-training.

blocks.en:
Several observations guided the final design. Held-out loss on the
training distribution was a poor predictor of downstream benchmark
rankings. Hyperparameters predicted by scaling laws exposed unstable
growth in mixture-of-experts (MoE) activations, requiring a separate
stabilization mechanism. Data augmentation methods effective in short
continued-pretraining runs required substantial revision before they
yielded gains in full-scale pretraining. Finally, reasoning traces alone
were insufficient for strong agentic performance: adding tool
interactions during pretraining improved subsequent supervised
fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL).

blocks.en: 2. Evaluation Methodology
blocks.zh: 2. 评价方法

blocks.en: 2.1 General Protocol
blocks.zh: 2.1 总议定书

blocks.en:
We evaluate each pretraining experiment across a broad range of
capabilities: factual knowledge, mathematics, reasoning, demanding
academic examinations, and long-context processing. Public benchmarks
support comparisons with other models, but do not fully cover the
capabilities relevant to our applications. Their scores can also
saturate over time, while repeated use increases the risk of overfitting
to these benchmarks. We therefore develop a substantial part of our
evaluation suite internally, guided by user needs and observed model
weaknesses.

We release WikiWebFacts and HardMultiQA together with the model to
support independent evaluation. Scores on generative benchmarks can be
sensitive to prompt wording, demonstrations, generation settings, and
grading procedures. We therefore validate new evaluation protocols

in settings. For public benchmarks, we first reproduce evaluations on
models with published results. We investigate discrepancies in either
direction and select a protocol that reasonably reproduces the published
results.

blocks.en: 2.2 Factual Knowledge

blocks.en:
A base model should both reason over supplied context and retain broad
knowledge of people, events, culture, science, and everyday subjects.
Examples of English-language factual knowledge benchmarks are TriviaQA,
Natural Questions, WebQuestions, and SimpleQA
[ 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 ]. Far fewer publicly available
benchmarks exist for Russian, and simply translating English-language
datasets into Russian does not address this gap. The knowledge most
relevant to users varies considerably across countries and languages,
particularly in areas such as history, geography, and culture.
Translated benchmarks fail to capture these differences.

blocks.en:
The model is an MoE Transformer with 80B total parameters and
approximately 3B active parameters per token. It contains 48 Transformer
blocks with hidden size 2048 and one multi-token-prediction layer. Each
MoE layer has 512 routed experts, of which ten are selected per token,
and one shared expert. Routing uses the auxiliary-loss-free balancing
approach of DeepSeek-V3 [ 22 ].

约每令牌3B活性参数. 它包含48变形器
带有隐藏大小 2048 和一个多键预测层的块。 每个
MOE层有512位路由专家 其中10位是每个符号的
和一个共享的专家。 运行使用辅助无损失平衡
[22]。

blocks.en:
Of the 48 attention layers, 36 use Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) and 12 use
full attention. One full-attention layer follows every three KDA layers.
Attention Residuals (AttnRes) replaces conventional residual summation
with learned weighting of representations across depth.
Section 4 details these choices.

blocks.en: 4.2.2 Muon

Muon (MomentUm Orthogonalized by Newton–Schulz) is an optimizer for
matrix-valued neural-network parameters. It computes momentum from
gradients and approximately orthogonalizes the momentum matrix using
Newton–Schulz iterations. This matrix-level transformation differs from
AdamW’s element-wise updates. Prior work reports comparable performance
at approximately half the training FLOPs of AdamW in a compute-optimal
setting [ 26 ]. Orthogonalization,
however, adds computation and communication to each optimizer step.

blocks.en:
In a fully sharded data-parallel (FSDP) setting, a parameter matrix may
be distributed across ranks, whereas orthogonalization requires the
complete matrix. Applying Newton–Schulz independently to FSDP shards is
not equivalent to orthogonalizing the full matrix. We first form work
units: MoE tensors are split along the expert axis, while other
two-dimensional weights each form one work unit. We estimate
orthogonalization cost from matrix dimensions and use
longest-processing-time (LPT) scheduling: units are sorted from most to
least expensive and assigned to the least-loaded compute groups. These
groups form stages with balanced work across GPUs, preventing a few
expensive matrices from delaying the entire step. Each matrix is
assigned to an owner GPU. Local shards are packed into communication
buffers and assembled in their original order at the owner. Within a
stage, momentum shards are gathered at their owners, orthogonalized,
split along the original FSDP shard boundaries, and returned to the
original ranks (Figure 9 ).

blocks.en: 4.2.3 Kimi Delta Attention
blocks.zh: 4.2.3 (中文(简体) ). 基米三角洲注意

blocks.en:
Full attention allows each token to access all preceding tokens
directly, but its key–value cache grows with context length. We combine
KDA [ 27 ] with full attention at
a 3:1 layer ratio. KDA compresses history into a fixed-size state
instead of storing separate keys and values for every token, so its
state memory does not grow with context length.
blocks.zh:
充分注意允许每个令牌访问所有前面的令牌
直接, 但是它的密钥- 值缓存会随着上下文长度增长 。 我们结合
KDA [27] 全力关注
a 3:1层比率。 KDA 压缩历史到固定大小状态
而不是为每个符号存储单独的密钥和值,所以
状态内存不会随上下文长度而增长。

blocks.en:
For each new token, KDA retrieves the value associated with its key,
compares it with the new value, and writes the difference into the
state. It thus incrementally corrects the state rather than replacing
it, while also allowing obsolete information to decay. Unlike the Gated
DeltaNet used in Qwen3-Next, which uses one decay coefficient per
attention head, KDA applies a separate coefficient to each row of the
state matrix. This allows more selective retention and forgetting.

blocks.en:
In experiments with 5–15B-parameter models, replacing Gated DeltaNet
with KDA reduced loss by approximately 0.02 and improved mathematics by
about 2–6 percentage points, MMLU-Pro CoT by 5 points, and educational
tasks and information extraction by 2–4 points. We therefore adopted

Full AttnRes attends to individual outputs of all earlier layers. We use

partial sum; each subsequent layer attends to this sum and completed
representations from preceding blocks. This reduces the number of
representations read by the kernel and the resulting memory traffic.

The model is pretrained on a mixture of natural, semi-synthetic, and
fully synthetic data. Natural sources include web pages, publicly
available source code, books, scientific papers, news, multilingual
data, open datasets and domain-specific resources such as legal codes,
clinical guidelines, and medical textbooks. We also include text
extracted from PDF and DjVu documents using optical character
recognition (OCR). Semi-synthetic data include augmented web pages and
generated or corrected solutions to problems drawn from existing
sources. Fully synthetic data consist of tasks and solutions generated
from scratch. The data undergo parsing, deduplication, and evaluation
benchmarks filtering. Figure 13 summarizes the corpus composition.

We collect web data using an in-house crawler. From Yandex’s crawled
search index, we select Russian- and English-language documents, as well
as the pages returned by Yandex Search in response to user queries. An
internal parser converts page content to Markdown. We then filter
documents by their quality using a cascade of models: a lightweight DSSM
classifier running on CPUs, a 0.5B encoder–decoder model, and, for
selected subsets, an 8B model based on YandexGPT 5 Lite Base.

blocks.en:
As described in Section 3, we extend the model’s context window to 256K

final reasoning stage. Natural documents approaching these lengths are
scarce, so we rely heavily on synthetic long-context data. Alongside
publicly available books, we include questions that require gathering
and combining information across an entire book, QA over spreadsheets
and other long structured inputs, and QA over collections of medical or
legal documents with each containing closely related terms. We also
include multi-hop search tasks with retrieved documents provided as
context.

Models acquire much of their factual knowledge during pretraining, and
filling the remaining gaps later can be difficult under a limited
compute budget. Gekhman et al. [35] find that models learn
unfamiliar facts more slowly than familiar ones during SFT and that
intensive training on new facts can increase the hallucination
frequency. We therefore treat factual knowledge as a core capability of
the base model, needed for both everyday questions and specialized
tasks. With a fixed training token budget, we aim to improve both the
coverage of relevant facts in the corpus and the model’s ability to
learn them.

investigated the effects of adding search-generated QA data to

blocks.en: 7.2.1 Mathematics

Our mathematical reasoning data combine public post-training datasets

original reasoning traces for some datasets and generate new ones for
others. We also extracted 45,000 Russian-language and 6,000

data in Section 6.8, we focus here on problems requiring advanced
mathematical reasoning and carefully validate both problem statements

Reference answers are unavailable for most problems, so we filter

least 0.5; otherwise, we discard the problem. This also removes many

solutions to the same problem.

blocks.en:
We constructed a synthetic corpus of challenging competitive-programming
problems and used strong models to generate solutions. The first
approach involved the model generating problems based on ideas from
computer science papers, including complete problem statements,
constraints, examples, and code for generating and checking tests.
Another approach was to generate a list of 1,000 algorithms and created
problems based on algorithms from this list. We further increased
difficulty by providing the model with two problems and their respective
solutions, then asking it to generate a new problem combining ideas from
both.

Our initial experiments focused on difficult standalone reasoning tasks.
We compared a checkpoint trained through the reasoning stage without
tool-use data against Qwen3A-35B-Base, applying the same agentic

blocks.en: 7.4.2 Search Questions

blocks.en:
We generate synthetic difficult multistep search questions from web
documents. Starting from a web page, the pipeline generates a factual
question asking for an entity name, searches for a new document using
that entity, extracts a related entity, and repeats. This forms a chain
of up to ten transitions. We then formulate a single question that
requires tracing the chain in reverse and is designed to take at least
eight search steps to solve. We use automated critique to check clarity,
answerability, and possible shortcuts, then revise the questions
accordingly (Figure 22).

blocks.en:
Agentic trajectories are stored as sequences of messages in a format
similar to the OpenAI chat format, extended with a model-specific meta
role: a trajectory is a sequence of messages with system, user,
assistant, tool, and meta roles; available tool definitions are supplied
separately in a tools field. Before tokenization, we serialize each
trajectory using our Jinja chat template. It specifies role prefixes and
the serialization of reasoning, tool descriptions, function calls, and
execution results.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en:
We have presented AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, an open
mixture-of-experts model trained from scratch. It surpasses our previous
proprietary Alice AI LLM in Russian-language factual knowledge while
using substantially fewer total and active parameters. It also
outperforms larger open base models on WikiWebFacts and HardMultiQA, and
comparable open base models on IMO-AnswerBench and LiveCodeBench under
zero-shot pass@k evaluation.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍了爱丽丝 -Foundation -80B -A3B -Base,一个开放的。
混合专家模式从零开始培训。 它超越了我们以前
以俄语掌握实际知识的Alice AI LLM
使用的总参数和活性参数要少得多。 还有
在WikiWebFacts和Hard MultiQA上超越更大的开放基模型,以及
海事组织-Answer Bench和LiveCode Bench的可比开放基础模型
0-shot pass@k 评价.

blocks.en:
Controlled ablations with a fixed training budget demonstrate that our
architecture improves overall performance relative to Qwen3-Next. We
also found that hyperparameter scaling-law predictions depend strongly
on the validation data used to fit them. Revising these datasets
produced learning-rate and batch-size predictions that improved
downstream performance over our baseline settings. An auxiliary loss on
MoE output activations enabled stable training at the predicted learning
rate.

blocks.en:
We provide a detailed description of how we analyzed and improved the
pretraining data pipeline, beginning with source collection and
filtering. These improvements increased the number of useful documents
retained for training. We introduced factual web data as a separate
component of the corpus, developed its retrieval and curation pipeline,
and adapted these methods to mathematics, programming, and STEM. We also
documented the augmentation strategies used across these domains.
blocks.zh:
我们详细描述了我们如何分析和改进
预训数据管道,从源收集和
过滤中。 这些改进增加了有用文件的数量
保留用于培训。 我们单独引入了真实的网络数据
开发其检索和保管管道,
并将这些方法适用于数学、编程和STEM。 我们也
记录了这些领域采用的增强战略。

blocks.en:
Finally, we describe the construction of the reasoning-stage dataset in
detail, from collecting and generating mathematical and programming
problems to producing and filtering reasoning traces and tool-use
trajectories. Training on reasoning traces improved performance on
reasoning benchmarks. Adding tool-use trajectories during pretraining
improved agentic benchmark performance when the same cold-start training
procedure was applied to the compared models.

The pretrained checkpoint is openly available under the Apache 2.0
license. We also release WikiWebFacts and HardMultiQA, two benchmarks
designed to assess factual knowledge relevant to Russian-speaking users,
together with their evaluation protocols. These releases support
independent evaluation and further research on pretraining data,
knowledge acquisition, reasoning, and agentic capabilities.
